category_title: Students with mild intellectual disability capable of logical leadership roles
minimal_context: Ben is sitting at a computer in the classroom to review his homework on Google Drive and set new learning goals.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Ben, it is time for self-evaluation. Please open your homework on Google Drive so we can set new goals and find out what you have to improve.

STUDENT: I don't want to look at the Drive. I don't want to do this right now.

TUTOR: What do you think you should pay more attention to for the next steps of your learning tasks?

STUDENT: Study. Good.

TUTOR: Can you write down a full sentence about your suggestions for your new goals?

STUDENT: (Sighs, looking frustrated) No. Just... read. Better.

options.A: Use desk carrels to provide areas of personal space and make a clear distinction between individual versus group activity areas in the classroom.
options.B: Provide a communication book composed of a typed conversational opener with a corresponding Picture Communication Symbol to use during the self-evaluation sessions.
options.C: Add a weekly school-to-home contingency to a behavior contract, requiring the student to meet a set number of academic targets per week to access a preferred weekend activity.
options.D: Teach the student to set a goal in his learning, find strategies to cope with challenges he faces, monitor his tasks, and evaluate each task after finishing it.
